values.raw: Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a cabin air, 1.0 atm ambient environment. This is the first FLEX test. The droplet remains in the FOV of all of the cameras for the entire test. The LLUV settings are not optimal and as a result the LLUV data are not reliable. The droplet likely disrupted at the end of the test coincident with flame extinction. The igniters were too bright and overexposed the HiBMS during ignition resulting in the inability to accurately measure the droplet diameter.

values.raw: Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a cabin air (0.21/0.79 O2/N2), 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet remains within the FOV of all the cameras and burns to diffusive extinction. values.raw: Free-floating heptane droplet in a nominally air (0.21/0.79 O2/N2, 1.0 atm) ambient environment. The droplet stays in the HiBMS FOV for the entire test including a long time after visible flame extinction. The flame oscillates before visible flame extinction, apparent in both the LLUV and color camera views. After flame extinction, the droplet vaporizes very vigorously with a nearly perfectly linear D^2 vs. time behavior. The vaporization rate is only slightly lower than the burning rate constant before flame extinction. The droplet vaporization rate then plateaus and this is coincident with the formation of a very large vapor cloud. This behavior is indicative of cool flame burning and extinction.

There is no extinction droplet diameter listed because of the limited time the droplet is in the HiBMS FOV and the disruptions in the droplet during the burn.

values.raw: Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.12/0.88 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet is nearly motionless after deployment/ignition, then starts to drift slowly E, but then chnages direction and quickly drifts W in HiBMS FOV. The droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV about 3/4ths of the way through the burn. The flame is very dim, but does appear to grow, reach a maximum and then decrease in size in response to the shrinking droplet. The extinction droplet diameter is based on extrapolating the droplet history to the time of extinction (as measured by the LLUV) using the burning rate constant measured from the last part of the droplet history while it is still in the HiBMS FOV. This is likely diffusive extinction with a significant contribution from radiative loss. The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment.
